facts.text: Machine recordings should include measurable light, visibility and weather where possible; precipitation and dust state; surface and grade; site type and scenario tag; and machine load and attachment state.

facts.text: A coarse human environmental tag such as "rain" is useful but cannot replace measurable context when environmental sensitivity becomes a safety claim.

facts.text: Missing or stale calibration and mount geometry prevent recorded images and points from being mapped reliably to machine or world coordinates.

facts.quote: lossy video changes detector outputs.

facts.text: Unrecorded packet or frame loss, or logging overload, can cause replay to reproduce a damaged log that engineers mistake for field behaviour.

facts.text: Event-triggered recording only, or collecting almost exclusively staged hazards, destroys the denominator needed to estimate false alarms per hour.

facts.text: Selecting machine recordings preferentially from good weather, day shifts and cooperative sites creates selection bias.

facts.text: Missing operator and HMI data prevents assessing whether a warning was useful.

facts.text: Missing binary and configuration provenance prevents tying a test result to an exact product state.
